payload.selection_rationale: Only one proposal was produced, and it is selected whole (`core`) rather than trimmed, because every piece of it is checkable against evidence already on record for this slice rather than against taste. The five risk-spike experiments (all run against real C:\Windows or a real hardlinked NTFS tree) support exactly the shape of fix chosen: TopLevelTracker.Moved is confirmed the only path that changes a row after Done (post-done-change-only-from-hardlinks), terminal states never change again (terminal-state-rows-never-change), at-risk rows are a small minority so a per-row mark stays meaningful rather than becoming noise on most rows (at-risk-rows-minority-on-full-c), and charging is deterministic so the acceptance test's setup is reproducible (hardlink-charge-deterministic-across-scans). The one no-go (report-captures-mid-scan-done-row) is honoured, not worked around: the design explicitly declines to touch --report schema 1 or add a new FsaWindowHook mode in this slice, which is the only way to respect a spike that measured the necessary hook/schema plumbing does not exist yet. The design also does not reopen the critique's M2 'Done is immutable' fix, which is recorded as impossible, and it takes the branch the failing test itself encodes (show a distinguishing suffix on the specific row) rather than a global relabelling. Against the build-check's finding that no field or per-row signal exists anywhere Core exposes to a display layer, the proposal's fix is the minimal one that creates exactly one: a single sticky bool set at the one place (Moved) that can observe both 'this row is already Done' and 'this change is non-zero', consumed by exactly one new case in the existing converter. The proposal's own over_engineering_flag correctly rejects four heavier, more 'complete' answers (a Beam-style timing enum, predictive at-risk marking, holding Done back, and a report/hook rebuild) as more than this bug needs, which is the signal a practice designer reporting against its own interest is supposed to give and which this composition takes at face value rather than second-guessing toward something more elaborate.

components.name: Revision bit in the tracker
components.responsibility: Inside TopLevelTracker.Moved, when a hardlink recharge changes a row's Bytes or OnDisk by a non-zero amount and that row's pending count is already 0 (Done), set that row's revised bit. Zero-byte moves and rows still reading are left unmarked. Once set for a scan it stays set. Written under the same lock/publish discipline Moved already uses for Bytes/OnDisk -- no new synchronisation.
components.key_interactions: Reached only from Scanner.Correct/Credit, the only call path the spike confirmed changes a row after Done. Publishes the bit into TopLevelRow on the same snapshot that already carries Bytes/OnDisk.

components.name: TopLevelRow.Revised and the restated Done promise
components.responsibility: Adds `bool Revised { get; init; }` defaulting to false -- an init-only member, not a new positional parameter, so existing construction sites still compile. Rewrites the TopLevelState.Done doc comment to state the promise plainly: listed and measured; until the scan ends it can still move, only through a hardlink recharge, and Revised is how that shows; after Completed or Cancelled it never changes again.
components.key_interactions: Read only by TopLevelRowText in App. WindowReport (schema 1) does not read it in this slice.

components.name: Done-revised title
components.responsibility: TitleOf gains one case, ordered before the fall-through: `TopLevelState.Done when row.Revised => $"{row.Name} (revised)"`. Ordinary Done rows and every other state's existing suffix are unchanged.
components.key_interactions: The single converter both the live 250ms-polled top-level list and the end-of-scan ShowFinalTopLevel list bind through; the build must confirm both actually go through it.

components.name: Tracker-level Facts (deterministic)
components.responsibility: Drive TopLevelTracker.Moved directly via InternalsVisibleTo to pin the flag's meaning independent of scanner timing: marks on a non-zero correction to a Done row; does not mark a still-reading row; does not mark a zero-byte move; marks both sides when a charge moves between two already-Done rows.
components.key_interactions: Sits next to the existing AnInPlaceCorrectionOfAnEarlierNameIsCreditedToThatNamesRow fact.

components.name: Bug project: acceptance plus a negative control
components.responsibility: The existing ADoneRowCorrectedInPlaceAfterItSettledReadsDifferentlyFromItsBareName stays unchanged and must pass. One control fact is added: a Done row nothing corrected must still read its bare name, guarding against the cheap wrong fix of suffixing every Done row.
components.key_interactions: Run through pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-063-DoneRowFinality/SL-063-DoneRowFinality.Tests.csproj, which must exit 0.

key_decisions.decision: Done promises the folder has been listed and measured, not that its figure is final until the scan ends; the one exception is a hardlink recharge, and it is shown on the row rather than hidden, held back, or masked by renaming/hedging every Done row.
key_decisions.rationale: Takes the 'show it' branch, not 'stop implying finality' as a global relabel. The failing test's only assertion is that a corrected row's title differs from its bare name -- it does not ask for a different state name or a global disclaimer. Spikes show changes are rare (0/126 rows per C:\Windows scan, 3 scans) against the one case validate saw, so marking every Done row would be noise on nearly all of them, and finality is real at scan end (0 changes across 48 scans post-Completed/Cancelled).

key_decisions.decision: The signal is a sticky per-row bool set inside TopLevelTracker.Moved -- under the lock Moved already uses -- only when the row was Done at that moment and the change was non-zero. The App never infers it by diffing successive polled snapshots.
key_decisions.rationale: Only the tracker knows under its own lock that a correction landed on a row that had settled. The App's 250ms poll can miss a correction landing in the same interval as Done, and diffing polls there would also conflate ordinary growth-while-reading with a genuine post-Done revision.

key_decisions.decision: Revised is an init-only member added to TopLevelRow, not a new positional/constructor parameter.
key_decisions.rationale: Extends the Core-to-App row contract without breaking existing construction sites in the tracker and its tests.

key_decisions.decision: Wording is the parenthetical suffix "(revised)", matching the existing style of other states' suffixes (e.g. "(reading...)").
key_decisions.rationale: Consistent with what is already on screen; borrows the 'revised figure' convention from published-statistics practice. Left explicitly changeable.

key_decisions.decision: No predictive 'may still change' mark on at-risk-but-not-yet-corrected rows, and Done is not held back until hardlinks resolve.
key_decisions.rationale: The critique's M2 fix (make Done immutable) is recorded as impossible and is not reopened here. At-risk rows are 3.0% of 932,531 Done rows, and actual post-Done changes were 0/126 per real scan -- a mark in advance would flag rows that almost never move, and NTFS itself only updates a directory-entry's size at the link through which the change was made (cited), which is exactly why this can only be shown after the fact, not predicted reliably beforehand.

key_decisions.decision: No change to --report schema 1 and no new FsaWindowHook mode in this slice; acceptance stops at the converter level plus a build-time check that both top-level list bindings go through TopLevelRowText.
key_decisions.rationale: The spike report-captures-mid-scan-done-row was no-go: the report writes only after the ending, carries no per-row field, and Q-016 already bars names from it. Building the hook mode and schema change this would need is out of proportion to a one-suffix fix; an aggregate revised count with no names is the smallest next step if window-level proof is ever wanted, and it is left for a later slice.

contracts.name: TopLevelRow.Revised
contracts.notes: bool, init-only, default false. True only once a hardlink recharge has changed this row's Bytes or OnDisk while its State was already Done; stays true for the rest of the scan. Never changes after Completed or Cancelled.
contracts.error_cases: A row whose correction landed before it reached Done is false, which is correct -- that figure was never presented as settled.

contracts.name: TopLevelTracker.Moved revision semantics
contracts.notes: Existing crediting behaviour is unchanged. Added: for each row Moved touches, if that row's pending count is 0 and the change to bytes or on-disk is non-zero, set its revised bit. An in-place correction (same row on both sides) marks it once; a charge moving between two already-Done rows marks both.
contracts.error_cases: Zero-byte moves do not mark. Moves on a still-reading row do not mark.

contracts.name: TopLevelRowText.TitleOf / Convert for Done
contracts.notes: Done+Revised=false gives row.Name, unchanged. Done+Revised=true gives "{row.Name} (revised)". Every other state's text is unchanged.
contracts.error_cases: Non-TopLevelRow or null input: unchanged from today's converter behaviour.

contracts.name: Acceptance command
contracts.notes: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-063-DoneRowFinality/SL-063-DoneRowFinality.Tests.csproj must exit 0, and the full Core.Tests suite through eng/dotnet.ps1 must stay green. Use eng/dotnet.ps1, never the machine's own dotnet, which only has SDK 8/9 (build-check measured exit 145 against global.json's pinned 10.0.100).
contracts.error_cases: If the bug fact passes in some runs and fails in others, the repro tree's correction can race '1-folder' settling; fix the ordering with ScanOptions.AfterFolder, do not widen the marking rule to hide it.

whats_new: the revision bit set inside TopLevelTracker.Moved when a Done row's figures change by a non-zero amount
one `TopLevelState.Done when row.Revised` case in TopLevelRowText.TitleOf printing "Name (revised)"
a rewritten doc comment on TopLevelState.Done stating what Done actually promises
deterministic tracker facts in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/TopLevelTests.cs covering the four Moved/Done/zero-byte/two-rows shapes
one negative-control fact in the SL-063 bug project: an uncorrected Done row still reads its bare name
whats_reused: the existing repro test and tree tests/bugs/SL-063-DoneRowFinality/DoneRowFinalityTests.cs, unchanged, as the acceptance criterion
TopLevelTracker.Moved as the single confirmed path that changes a row after Done
the tracker's existing lock and publish path for Bytes/OnDisk, carrying the new bit alongside them
the existing parenthetical suffix convention in TopLevelRowText
the window's existing 250ms DispatcherTimer poll and ShowFinalTopLevel binding
InternalsVisibleTo from Core to Core.Tests for tracker-level facts
eng/dotnet.ps1's repo-local SDK bootstrap, required on this machine to build or run anything (machine dotnet only has SDK 8/9)

cases.shape: a hardlink recharge (Moved) changes bytes/on-disk on a row already Done, by a non-zero amount
cases.why: the exact defect the repro proves; without this the flag's core trigger is unexercised

cases.shape: Moved changes a row that is still Reading (pending count > 0)
cases.why: guards against marking rows that never claimed to be settled -- a wrong implementation could set the bit on any Moved regardless of state

cases.shape: Moved reports a zero-byte change on an already-Done row
cases.why: confirms the non-zero guard, so no-op recharges don't create false revision noise

cases.shape: a hardlink charge moves between two rows that are both already Done
cases.why: design requires both rows marked; a one-sided implementation would silently leave the source or target unmarked

cases.shape: a Done row nothing ever corrected
cases.why: negative control against the cheap wrong fix of suffixing every Done row, which would make the marker meaningless noise

cases.shape: a Done row whose figures were corrected in place after it settled
cases.why: this is the failing acceptance test itself; TitleOf must stop returning the bare name for this row

cases.shape: TitleOf is given Revised=true paired with each non-Done TopLevelState
cases.why: Revised can only reach true via Done in the tracker, but TitleOf is a pure converter -- wrong case-arm ordering could leak the suffix onto a Reading/Cancelled row or swallow it entirely

cases.behaviour: show the revision suffix in the actual window
cases.shape: the same row rendered through both the live 250ms-poll top-level list and the end-of-scan ShowFinalTopLevel list
cases.why: if either binding path uses a different template than TopLevelRowText, the suffix silently never appears in one of the two views despite a green unit test on the converter alone

cases.shape: the correction lands in the same ~250ms interval in which the row first reaches Done, so the person never actually saw the unrevised figure on screen
cases.why: Core has no signal for 'was this actually painted before the correction'; the design accepts this small over-marking rather than building UI-paint-timing instrumentation, so it is a considered omission, not an oversight

cases.shape: the bug-project repro tree's hardlink correction may race the scan's own settling of the '1-folder' row
cases.why: only one engine run is on record; if the correction can land before the row reaches Done in some runs the test flakes instead of reliably reproducing the bug -- the design calls for repeated runs (~20) before trusting a single green pass

architecture_rules.name: the revision wording lives in exactly one place
architecture_rules.because: Core exposes only the bool signal; if the suffix text is duplicated into Core or into a second App file, the two copies drift and a row can end up shown as final in one place while marked revised in another

architecture_rules.name: only the tracker's Moved path sets the revision bit
architecture_rules.because: only Moved's crediting path, under the tracker's existing lock, can observe both that the row was already Done and that the change is non-zero; setting it elsewhere risks marking a row before it settled or racing the credit

architecture_rules.name: the mid-scan report stays untouched by this slice
architecture_rules.because: the spike report-captures-mid-scan-done-row found the report is written only after the ending and has no per-row field, and Q-016 bars names from it; wiring Revised in here without the hook/schema work that spike found missing would be silently inert or wrong

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Official statistics publication, and streaming-dataflow late firings
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Publish, then revise in place with a lasting mark: a figure goes out when its inputs are in; a rare late input updates that same figure where it stands and marks it revised; the mark stays, and there is a known point after which no further revision happens.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: A Done row is a published figure. A hardlink recharge is a late input the publisher could not withhold Done for, since making Done immutable (the critique's M2 fix) is recorded as impossible. Scan end is the final release. What transfers is the marking rule -- mark only revisions of figures already published, keep the mark, never mark ahead of time -- which keeps the mark rare enough to mean something. What does not transfer is the heavier machinery of the source domain: multiple timing states, accumulating-vs-discarding modes, a revision history. One bool covers a single confirmed cause.

invariants.precondition: revisions are rare compared with publications, so a mark stays signal rather than noise
invariants.evidence: spike post-done-change-only-from-hardlinks: 0/126 rows changed after Done in each of 3 real C:\Windows scans, control 0/2001; validate saw one such row across a whole drive

invariants.precondition: there is a final release after which no figure changes, so the mark and numbers are stable at the end
invariants.evidence: spike terminal-state-rows-never-change: 0 row changes across 48 real C:\Windows scans, including 14 genuine Cancels, 5 within 0.8s of a hardlink fix-up

invariants.precondition: a revision has a single known cause, so one unqualified mark is enough
invariants.evidence: spike post-done-change-only-from-hardlinks: TopLevelTracker.Moved, reached only from Scanner.Correct/Credit, is the only path that changes a row after its pending count reaches 0

invariants.precondition: whoever applies the revision knows at that moment the figure was already published (row already Done)
invariants.evidence: Done-ness lives in the tracker as pending-count-0, and Moved runs inside the tracker, but the build must confirm Moved can read that row's pending count under the same lock it uses to credit bytes/on-disk

invariants.precondition: in the repro tree, the correction reliably lands after '1-folder' has settled, so the acceptance test is deterministic under the 'only if Done' rule
invariants.evidence: only one engine run is on record for the repro; it passed the Done+64MiB assertions that run, but a single run does not prove the ordering is not racy

prior_art.pattern: On NTFS a hardlinked file's directory-entry size is updated only at the link through which the change was made, so a listing can report a stale size for the other names -- which is why a later probe corrects the charge and why that cannot be prevented, only shown.

Disk-usage tools that count each hardlinked file once must pick which name carries the bytes; the row charged then depends on which name is seen first, which is what makes a late correction land on a row that already looked final.

A results table that keeps showing stale state after the underlying data changed confuses the user until a re-scan; the fix there was to refresh in place. Here the figure is already refreshed in place, and the missing half is telling the person it moved.
Streaming results with late data: a result emitted as on-time can be refined by a later firing, and each emitted result carries its timing so consumers can tell a late revision from the first answer.
prior_art.where: Apache Beam / Google Cloud Dataflow PaneInfo timing

prior_art.pattern: Published figures are revised in place and marked with a lasting footnote (preliminary / revised), never silently overwritten and never held back until nothing could change.
prior_art.where: US BLS / national statistics release conventions

taste_disagreements: The exact suffix wording "(revised)" versus an alternative like "(updated)" or "(corrected)" is unsettled cosmetics -- the proposal itself calls it changeable in an hour and picked it only for consistency with the existing "(reading...)" style.
open_questions: Does 'show it, don't imply finality' cover only the top-level list rows the failing test and validate's C:\Windows observation describe, or should folder-tree drill-down nodes (built from ScanStore after the scan) also carry a revision mark? This design covers only the top-level list, matching the bug's own framing ('the window prints no suffix'), but a person could decide the promise should extend to the tree view too.
channeled_experts: Tyler Akidau: watermarks and late firings (answers that arrive late are marked, not suppressed)
Official-statistics revision practice (preliminary and revised footnotes)
NTFS hardlink semantics as documented by Microsoft (directory-entry size staleness)

proposals.note: Selected whole: the fix is one sticky bool set at the single confirmed mutation path (TopLevelTracker.Moved), one init-only field, one TitleOf case -- grounded in all four go-spikes and respecting the one no-go by declining to touch the report/hook layer. Its over_engineering_flag correctly rejected four heavier alternatives (timing enum, predictive at-risk marking, holding Done back, report/hook rebuild) as more than this bug needs.

payload.coherence_check: Only one proposal was produced for SL-063, so there is no cross-proposal composition to check -- nothing here has been argued with by another piece, and that is the honest state to hand the reviewer. What I did check was internal coherence between this single design's own decisions and the evidence already on record for this slice: the decision to mark only via Moved matches the spike finding that Moved is the only path that changes a row after Done; the decision not to predict at-risk rows in advance matches the spike finding that at-risk rows are a small minority (3.0%) and actual post-Done changes are near-zero (0/126 per real scan); the decision not to touch --report schema 1 or FsaWindowHook matches the spike's own no-go, which found the hook/schema plumbing this would need does not exist yet; and the decision not to reopen 'Done is immutable' matches the critique's own finding that fix is impossible. No contradiction requiring a redesigned seam turned up between the design's claims and the recorded spikes, the build-check's finding (no per-row signal exists anywhere today), or the answered questions block -- none of Q-001 through Q-016 touch this decision, so nothing there overrides it either. The one thing this composition added beyond the proposal itself is the architecture_rules and the case matrix, both derived directly from invariants the proposal already stated in prose (single-writer bit, single-source wording, report untouched) but had not written in a form that fails.
